# Mathematical symbols — provenance report

<!-- Generated from authored/mathematical-symbols.json by scripts/authored_decks.py. Do not edit: change the dossier and rebuild. -->

**Deck:** [`decks/mathematical-symbols.ttl`](../decks/mathematical-symbols.ttl) · **Cards:** 45 · **Licence:** [CC0 1.0 Universal](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) · **Compiled by:** Anton Wiklund · **Created:** 2026-10-04

45 common mathematical symbols and what they mean: logic (∀, ∃, ¬, ∧, ∨, ⇒, ⇔), sets and number sets (∈, ⊆, ⊂, ∪, ∩, ℕ, ℝ …), relations (≠, ≈, ∝, ≤, ≡ …), operators (∑, ∏, √, ∫, ∂, ∇, n! …) and the constants π, e and i, plus ∞. Front: the symbol, in a short expression where it needs one (⌊x⌋, g ∘ f); back: its meaning in English and Swedish. ⊂ is read as proper subset and ℕ includes 0. Checked against Wikidata, the Unicode Character Database and the English and Swedish Wikipedia.

## Licensing

The only content source is Wikidata, whose structured data is CC0: the link from each symbol to its concept, the concept names in English and Swedish and the ISO 80000-2 item records come from it, and the card texts are the compiler's own wording of the meanings, so the deck is CC0 1.0. The Unicode Character Database (Unicode License v3, permissive but not a licence the builder knows), ISO 80000-2 (all rights reserved), the English Wikipedia glossary and article and the Swedish Wikipedia list and articles (CC BY-SA 4.0) were used for verification only: they confirmed the meanings and that the Swedish readings the compiler chose are the usual ones. The Swedish readings that Wikidata does not hold ("för alla", "är ett element i", "mängddifferens" …) are standard terminology, single words or set phrases that are not protected expression; no sentence, note, example, table layout or selection was copied from any of these sources, and notes whose first drafts followed a Wikipedia sentence closely were rewritten in round 3. The selection follows the editor's brief, grouped broadly as ISO 80000-2's clauses as recorded in Wikidata; it is not the selection of the Swedish or English Wikipedia list. Meanings of symbols and the names of mathematical concepts are facts, not copyrightable expression.

## Method

1. Who did the work: Anton Wiklund compiled this deck with the help of AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic), which did the research, drafting and cross-checking at his direction. The cards were checked by machine (the Unicode Character Database, live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators) and in independent review rounds by further Claude agents, each logged under Quality control with its findings and how they were resolved. Anton Wiklund reviews every deck in full before it is released.
2. Candidate symbols: the library editor's brief named about 45 symbols in five groups (logic, sets, relations, operators, constants). For each, Wikidata was searched for the items that carry the symbol as Unicode character (P487) (query 1) and the statements of those items (query 2), which link character items to concepts through notation (P913), depicts (P180), has use (P366) or symbolizes (P4878).
3. ISO 80000-2 as recorded in Wikidata: query 3 listed every Wikidata item described by ISO 80000-2:2019 (Q109490582) with the item number (P958 section, e.g. "2-6.8") and the standard's verbal equivalent (P1810 subject named as, e.g. "B is properly included in A"). Every card's concept was matched to one of these records where one exists (all but ∝, and ∫ via the indefinite integral item); this is what the evidence calls the ISO item number. The standard's own tables could not be read: the ISO Online Browsing Platform answered 403 (https://www.iso.org/obp/ui/en/#iso:std:iso:80000:-2:ed-2:v1:en), and the publisher's free preview (query 10) ends after clause 4. From the preview only clause 4's sentence on mathematical constants (e, π, i) is used.
4. Concepts and labels: query 4 fetched, for the chosen concept items, the English and Swedish labels, Swedish aliases, P487, the notation items with their characters and the ISO records; query 5 the Swedish Wikipedia article title and the character items linked to each concept; query 6 the P487, P913 and P1343 statements that the build checks. While doing so the Query Service was found to return "ℜ" (U+211C) as P487 of the set of real numbers (Q1174982) where the Wikidata API returns "ℝ" (U+211D) (queries 7 and 8); see round 0.
5. Characters: UnicodeData.txt of the Unicode Character Database 18.0.0 was downloaded (query 11) and the script ucd.py (query 12) printed the line of every character used on a front, which fixed the exact code point (for example U+2223 DIVIDES rather than U+007C VERTICAL LINE for "a ∣ b", U+2216 SET MINUS rather than the backslash for "A ∖ B") and gave the official character name as a check of the meaning.
6. Independent check in English: the wikitext of the English Wikipedia "Glossary of mathematical symbols" (query 11) was searched with grep_en.py (query 13) and grep (query 14) for the entry of each symbol; each card's meaning agrees with it (∠, π, e and i are not in the glossary). The English Wikipedia article "Natural number" (query 15) was read for the ISO convention on 0.
7. Swedish: the Swedish Wikipedia "Lista över matematiska symboler" (query 11, wikitext extracted by query 20) and Swedish Wikipedia articles on the concepts (svwiki.py, query 16: 46 titles tried, 41 found, two of them redirects to the same article; plain-text extracts with revision ids; grep_sv.py, query 17; in round 3 also "Skilt från-tecknet", query 24) were read to confirm the Swedish terms. The Swedish backs are standard Swedish terminology chosen by the compiler: single words or set phrases, not protected expression. Where Wikidata has the term as an sv label or alias, the back follows it (konjunktion, disjunktion, negation, implikation, delmängd, union, snitt, tomma mängden, mindre/större än eller lika med, summa, produkt, kvadratrot, absolutbelopp, golvfunktion, takfunktion, fakultet, sammansatt funktion, nablaoperatorn, imaginära enheten, oändlighet, vinkel, Eulers tal, "inte lika med-tecknet" for ≠); the other readings (för alla, det finns, implicerar, om och endast om, är ett element i, äkta delmängd, mängddifferens, kongruent modulo n, delar, proportionell mot, ungefär lika med, plus eller minus) are the usual ones, which the Swedish list and articles only confirmed; no sentences, notes or selection were taken from them. Swedish lower-case style is used throughout (Wikidata's "Partiell derivata" is written "partiell derivata"), named sets and constants with an adjective take the Swedish double definite form ("de naturliga talen", "den tomma mängden", "den imaginära enheten"), and Swedish decimal commas are used in the Swedish notes.
8. Writing the cards: the backs are the compiler's own short wording of the meaning, in the form in which the symbol is read ("is an element of", "för alla"), with the concept name in brackets where the reading alone is a bare word ("and (conjunction)"). Fronts are text in no language (zxx). A symbol is shown in a short expression where it has another common meaning or could be mistaken for another character: "A ∖ B", "a ≡ b (mod n)", "a ∣ b", "|x|", "⌊x⌋", "⌈x⌉", "n!", "g ∘ f". The constants π, e and i have the front note "a mathematical constant" so that e and i are not read as variables (or e as the elementary charge). Notes give a formula, an example or the convention used, in the compiler's own words and with examples of the compiler's own choosing; examples are introduced with "for example" / "till exempel", and notes that are sentences end with a full stop. Expression fronts get expression readings ("absolute value of x", "floor of x", "g composed with f").
9. Checks: every card has Wikidata checks run by the builder against live Wikidata: the symbol (P487 on the concept or on its character item), the link between character and concept (P913, P180 or P366), a stable label in English or Swedish, and the concept's ISO 80000-2 record (P1343 Q109490582). Checks were left out where Wikidata disagrees with the card or the Query Service returns a different character (⊂ on subset, ℝ, e); see round 0.
10. Left out: ⊥ (U+22A5 UP TACK is also the logical constant false, and Unicode has a separate U+27C2 PERPENDICULAR, so the front would be ambiguous between characters and meanings); ≪ and ≫ (no Swedish source for the reading was found beyond the plain translation; the Swedish Wikipedia search for "mycket mindre än", query 22, gave 186 hits, the first ten all outside mathematics); ∄, ∃!, ∴, ∵ and ∮ (not in the brief and outside ISO 80000-2's tables as recorded in Wikidata); ≡ alone (identity, congruence or logical equivalence) and the bare vertical bar (absolute value, divides, such that), which appear only in expressions that fix one meaning.

## Selection

45 symbols in five groups, chosen from the library editor's brief and grouped broadly as ISO 80000-2:2019's clauses (as recorded in Wikidata): logic ∀ ∃ ¬ ∧ ∨ ⇒ ⇔ (7); sets ∈ ∉ ∅ ⊆ ⊂ ∪ ∩ ∖ and the number sets ℕ ℤ ℚ ℝ ℂ (13); relations and geometry ≠ ≈ ∝ ≤ ≥, congruence modulo n, divides, parallel and angle (9); operators ∑ ∏ √ ± |x| ⌊x⌋ ⌈x⌉ n! ∘ ∫ ∂ ∇ (12); the constants π, e and i and the symbol ∞ (4). Each is a symbol a student meets in upper-secondary or first-year university mathematics and has one standard meaning given the front. Where usage differs the card states the convention in its note: ⊂ is a proper subset (with ⊆ for subset), as in the Swedish Wikipedia list and the reading that pairs ⊂ with ⊆, and ℕ includes 0, as in ISO 80000-2 and Skolverket's terminology. Left out: ⊥ (two characters, and also "false"), ≪ and ≫, ∄, ∃!, ∴, ∵, ∮, and symbols whose meaning depends on context without a disambiguating expression (≡ alone, |, ~, ×, Δ, →).

## Queries

**1. Items whose Unicode character (P487) is one of the candidate symbols, with en and sv labels (sh run.sh q1, which runs: curl -s -H "User-Agent: solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -H "Accept: text/csv" --data-urlencode query@q1.rq https://query.wikidata.org/sparql > q1.csv, in <scratch>)** (Wikidata: mathematical concepts, their symbols, labels and ISO 80000-2 records)

```
SELECT ?sym ?item ?en ?sv WHERE {
  VALUES ?sym { "∀" "∃" "∄" "¬" "∧" "∨" "⇒" "⇔" "∈" "∉" "⊂" "⊆" "∪" "∩" "∅" "ℕ" "ℤ" "ℚ" "ℝ" "ℂ" "∖" "\\" "≠" "≈" "≡" "≤" "≥" "∝" "≪" "≫" "∑" "∏" "∫" "∮" "∂" "∇" "√" "!" "|" "⌊" "⌋" "⌈" "⌉" "±" "∘" "π" "e" "i" "∞" "∥" "⊥" "×" "→" "↦" }
  ?item wdt:P487 ?sym .
  OPTIONAL { ?item rdfs:label ?en FILTER(LANG(?en) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?item rdfs:label ?sv FILTER(LANG(?sv) = "sv") }
}
ORDER BY ?sym

```

**2. Item-valued statements of those items, to find the concept each character is linked to (sh run.sh q2)** (Wikidata: mathematical concepts, their symbols, labels and ISO 80000-2 records)

```
SELECT ?sym ?char ?prop ?propLabel ?val ?valEn ?valSv WHERE {
  VALUES ?sym { "∀" "∃" "∄" "¬" "∧" "∨" "⇒" "⇔" "∈" "∉" "⊂" "⊆" "∪" "∩" "∅" "∖" "≠" "≈" "≡" "≤" "≥" "∝" "≪" "≫" "∑" "∏" "∫" "∮" "∂" "∇" "√" "⌊" "⌋" "⌈" "⌉" "±" "∘" "∞" "∥" "⊥" }
  ?char wdt:P487 ?sym .
  ?char ?p ?val .
  ?prop wikibase:directClaim ?p .
  FILTER(?prop NOT IN (wd:P487, wd:P4213, wd:P31, wd:P361, wd:P5949))
  FILTER(isIRI(?val))
  OPTIONAL { ?val rdfs:label ?valEn FILTER(LANG(?valEn) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?val rdfs:label ?valSv FILTER(LANG(?valSv) = "sv") }
  SERVICE wikibase:label { bd:serviceParam wikibase:language "en". }
}
ORDER BY ?sym ?char

```

**3. Every item described by ISO 80000-2:2019 (Q109490582) with its section (P958) and subject named as (P1810) qualifiers (sh run.sh q3)** (Wikidata: mathematical concepts, their symbols, labels and ISO 80000-2 records)

```
SELECT ?item ?en ?sv ?qual ?qualLabel ?qv WHERE {
  ?item p:P1343 ?st .
  ?st ps:P1343 wd:Q109490582 .
  OPTIONAL { ?st ?pq ?qv . ?qual wikibase:qualifier ?pq . }
  OPTIONAL { ?item rdfs:label ?en FILTER(LANG(?en) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?item rdfs:label ?sv FILTER(LANG(?sv) = "sv") }
  SERVICE wikibase:label { bd:serviceParam wikibase:language "en". }
}
ORDER BY ?qv

```

**4. Labels, Swedish aliases, P487, notations and ISO records of the chosen concept items (sh run.sh q4)** (Wikidata: mathematical concepts, their symbols, labels and ISO 80000-2 records)

```
SELECT ?item ?en ?sv ?svAliases ?unicode ?notation ?notationLabel ?notationChar ?isoSection ?isoNamedAs WHERE {
  VALUES ?item { wd:Q191081 wd:Q1651704 wd:Q190558 wd:Q7881229 wd:Q220433 wd:Q126695 wd:Q773483
    wd:Q655288 wd:Q109610770 wd:Q226183 wd:Q177646 wd:Q59489332 wd:Q185359 wd:Q185837 wd:Q845126
    wd:Q28777634 wd:Q47007735 wd:Q47005650 wd:Q1174982 wd:Q26851286
    wd:Q110013332 wd:Q26161438 wd:Q11668618 wd:Q55935291 wd:Q110064509 wd:Q110064531 wd:Q3773677
    wd:Q109497082 wd:Q110064552 wd:Q53875 wd:Q205034 wd:Q11352
    wd:Q218005 wd:Q901718 wd:Q134237 wd:Q260387 wd:Q120812 wd:Q56860783 wd:Q12718884 wd:Q120976
    wd:Q244761 wd:Q80091 wd:Q8437543 wd:Q186475 wd:Q334508 wd:Q167 wd:Q82435 wd:Q193796 wd:Q205 }
  OPTIONAL { ?item rdfs:label ?en FILTER(LANG(?en) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?item rdfs:label ?sv FILTER(LANG(?sv) = "sv") }
  OPTIONAL { SELECT ?item (GROUP_CONCAT(?a; separator=" | ") AS ?svAliases) WHERE { ?item skos:altLabel ?a FILTER(LANG(?a) = "sv") } GROUP BY ?item }

```

```
"""Print the UnicodeData.txt line of every character on the deck's fronts."""

data = {}
```

```
"""Fetch the plain-text content and revision id of Swedish Wikipedia articles (verification of Swedish terms).
Usage: python3 svwiki.py   -> writes svwiki-articles.json"""
import json, urllib.parse, urllib.request, pathlib

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).parent
UA = "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)"
TITLES = ["Delmängd", "Kongruens (talteori)", "Moduloräkning", "Delbarhet", "Proportionalitet (matematik)", "E (tal)",
          "Imaginära enheten", "Golv- och takfunktionerna", "Heltalsdel", "Sammansatt funktion", "Partiell derivata",
          "Nablaoperatorn", "Parallell (matematik)", "Vinkel", "Olikhet", "Likhetstecken", "Naturliga tal",
          "Mängddifferens", "Differens (mängdlära)", "Element (mängdlära)", "Absolutbelopp", "Fakultet (matematik)",
          "Allkvantifikator", "Existenskvantifikator", "Implikation", "Ekvivalens (logik)", "Konjunktion (logik)",
          "Disjunktion", "Negation", "Union (matematik)", "Snitt", "Tomma mängden", "Oändlighet", "Pi", "Integral",
          "Summa", "Produkt (matematik)", "Kvadratrot", "Plus–minustecken", "Heltal", "Rationella tal", "Reella tal",
          "Komplexa tal", "Ungefär lika med", "Skilt från-tecken", "Mycket mindre än"]
out = {}
for t in TITLES:
    q = urllib.parse.urlencode({"action": "query", "prop": "extracts|revisions", "explaintext": 1, "rvprop": "ids",
                                "redirects": 1, "format": "json", "formatversion": 2, "titles": t})
    req = urllib.request.Request("https://sv.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?" + q, headers={"User-Agent": UA})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as r:
        page = json.load(r)["query"]["pages"][0]
    out[t] = {"title": page.get("title"), "missing": page.get("missing", False),
              "revid": (page.get("revisions") or [{}])[0].get("revid"), "text": page.get("extract", "")}
    print(t, "->", page.get("title"), "missing" if page.get("missing") else (page.get("revisions") or [{}])[0].get("revid"))
(HERE / "svwiki-articles.json").write_text(json.dumps(out, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")

```

```
import json, pathlib, re, sys
d = json.loads((pathlib.Path(__file__).parent / "svwiki-articles.json").read_text())
pats = {
 "Delmängd": r"äkta|⊂|⊆|⊊", "Modulär aritmetik": r"kongruent|≡", "Delbarhet": r"delar|∣|\|",
 "Proportionalitet (matematik)": r"∝|proportionell", "E (tal)": r"Eulers|Nepers|bas", "Imaginära enheten": r"imaginära enheten|i2|i²|−1",
 "Golv- och takfunktionerna": r"golv|tak|⌊|⌈|största|minsta", "Sammansatt funktion": r"∘|sammansatt|efter",
 "Partiell derivata": r"∂|partiell", "Nablaoperatorn": r"∇|nabla|del", "Parallell (matematik)": r"∥|parallell",
 "Vinkel": r"∠", "Olikhet": r"≠|≪|≫|mycket|skild|inte lika", "Likhetstecken": r"≈|≠|ungefär|skilt", "Naturliga tal": r"ISO|noll|0",
 "Differens": r"∖|\\\\|mängddifferens|differens", "Absolutbelopp": r"absolutbelopp|\|", "Fakultet (matematik)": r"fakultet|!",
 "Allkvantifikator": r"∀|för alla", "Existenskvantifikator": r"∃|det finns|existerar", "Implikation": r"⇒|→|medför|implicerar|om .* så",
 "Ekvivalens (logik)": r"⇔|↔|om och endast om", "Konjunktion (logik)": r"∧|och", "Disjunktion": r"∨|eller", "Negation": r"¬|icke|inte",
 "Union (matematik)": r"∪", "Snitt": r"∩", "Tomma mängden": r"∅", "Oändlighet": r"∞", "Pi": r"omkrets|diameter", "Integral": r"∫",
 "Summa": r"∑|Σ|summa", "Produkt (matematik)": r"∏|Π", "Kvadratrot": r"√", "Plus–minustecken": r"±|plus eller minus|plus-minus",
 "Heltal": r"ℤ|Z", "Rationella tal": r"ℚ|Q", "Reella tal": r"ℝ|R", "Komplexa tal": r"ℂ|C", "Närmevärde": r"≈|ungefär",
}
for k, v in d.items():
    t = v["text"]; title = v["title"]
    if v["missing"] or title not in pats: continue
    sents = re.split(r"(?<=[.\n])\s*", t)
    hits = [s.strip() for s in sents if re.search(pats[title], s)][:4]
    print(f"== {title} ({v['revid']})")
    for h in hits: print("   ", h[:300])
```

## Quality control

6 rounds, 37 findings: 35 fixed, 0 rejected after checking, 2 needing no change. Every card's Wikidata checks (148 in all) are re-run against live Wikidata by `scripts/authored_decks.py check` before every build.

### Round 0: Sources, licences and machine checks: every symbol's character against the Unicode Character Database, its meaning against Wikidata and the English Wikipedia glossary, the Swedish terms against Wikidata sv labels and the Swedish Wikipedia; ambiguity of each front. (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — authoring agent, machine checks · **Scope:** All 45 cards, the sources and the deck metadata.

All 45 meanings agree between Wikidata and at least one independent source (the English glossary for 41; the ISO preview and the Swedish Wikipedia for π, e and i; the Unicode character name for ∠), and every front character was confirmed in UnicodeData.txt. ISO 80000-2's tables could not be read, so ISO is cited only through Wikidata's records and the preview's clause 4. Three Wikidata checks were left out because Wikidata (or its Query Service) disagrees with the card; eight fronts were given a short expression to remove ambiguity; ⊥, ≪ and ≫ were left out.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| proper-subset | Two conventions for ⊂: the English glossary gives both (subset possibly equal, or proper subset); the Swedish Wikipedia list gives "A ⊂ B betyder: A ⊆ B men A ≠ B". Wikidata puts P487 "⊂" on subset (Q177646, ISO 2-6.7), not on proper subset (Q59489332, ISO 2-6.8, no symbol). The brief asked whether ISO 80000-2 uses ⊂ for a proper subset; the ISO tables could not be read, so this is not claimed. | Back "is a proper subset of", with ⊆ as its own card for subset; the note states the convention, the other usage and the unambiguous ⊊. No P487 check on Q177646; the card checks Q59489332's label and ISO record and the character item ⊂. | fixed |
| real-numbers | The Wikidata Query Service returns "ℜ" (U+211C BLACK-LETTER CAPITAL R, the real-part symbol) as P487 of the set of real numbers (Q1174982), in CSV and in JSON (query 7), while the Wikidata API returns "ℝ" (U+211D) for the same statement (query 8). The CSV output also showed English labels "ℨ" for the ℤ character items whose API labels are "ℤ". | The card's front is ℝ (U+211D, confirmed in UnicodeData.txt and the API). The builder reads the Query Service, so the P487 check is replaced by the character item's link (Q87523867 depicts Q1174982), its en label and its ISO record. | fixed |
| e | Wikidata's P487 for Euler's number (Q82435) is "𝑒" (U+1D452 MATHEMATICAL ITALIC SMALL E), not the plain letter on the front; ISO 80000-2 clause 4 prints constants upright. | Front is the plain letter e (with the note "a constant"); no P487 check, the card checks the en label and the sv alias "Eulers tal". | fixed |
| congruent-modulo | ≡ alone has several meanings (identity, congruence modulo n, logical equivalence: English glossary; Wikidata's ≡ character item depicts logical equivalence and "if and only if"); Unicode names it IDENTICAL TO. | Front "a ≡ b (mod n)", which has one meaning; the ISO record (2-8.18, congruence of integers) and the triple-bar notation are checked. | fixed |
| divides | The vertical bar is absolute value, divides and "such that"; Unicode has a separate U+2223 DIVIDES. Wikidata's "divides" (Q109497082) has no symbol statement. | Front "a ∣ b" with U+2223; absolute value has its own card "\|x\|" with U+007C. Checked by label and ISO record only. | fixed |
| set-difference | The Swedish list writes set difference with a plain backslash "\"; the brief also wrote "\". Unicode has U+2216 SET MINUS, which Wikidata records for set difference (Q845126). | Front "A ∖ B" with U+2216, in an expression so it is not read as a stray slash. | fixed |
| proportional-to | The Swedish Wikipedia article says the relation is usually written y ∼ x and "mer sällan" y ∝ x ("mest i engelskspråkig litteratur"); Wikidata lists ∝, ~ and :: as notations of proportionality, which has no ISO 80000-2 record in Wikidata. | Kept ∝ (the brief, Unicode PROPORTIONAL TO, the glossary); the note mentions the Swedish y ∼ x. No ISO check. | fixed |
| natural-numbers | Whether 0 ∈ ℕ varies: the English glossary gives {1, 2, …} "or sometimes" {0, 1, 2, …}; Wikidata's ℕ item is the set of non-negative integers with ISO named-as "the set of positive integers and zero"; the English article says ISO 80000-2 includes 0; the Swedish list and article (Skolverket) include 0. | Back "the natural numbers"; the note states that 0 is included here and that some authors start at 1. | fixed |
| partial-derivative | Wikidata's sv label is "Partiell derivata" with a capital P; ∂ alone also denotes a boundary (glossary, Wikidata P366). | Swedish back in lower case per Swedish style (as the Swedish article writes it); no sv label check.
